findings.title: Settings policy module cleanly centralizes the auto-memory and setting-sources decision
findings.description: The new `providers/sdk/settings.py` module is a well-scoped single source of truth for the settings policy that previously lived inline in `provider.py` and was absent from the session builder. The `SdkSettings` TypedDict, `sdk_settings_options`, `pipeline_setting_sources`, and the two `*_SETTING_SOURCES` constants give every automated SDK path one entry point. The provider and the session builder both call into it, and the per-path test in `tests/providers/sdk/test_settings_policy.py` drives each real builder and asserts the resulting sources and auto-memory flag — this is the right shape for a policy that must not drift across call sites.

findings.title: Background-task ledger and dispatch-turn bookkeeping are properly separated from I/O
findings.description: `sdk_turns.py` is pure bookkeeping: `BackgroundLedger` tracks task lifecycle, `DispatchTurns` accumulates response text and turn state, and `is_own_result` classifies `ResultMessage.origin`. No client, no I/O, no async. The `SDKExecutionSession` in `sdk_session.py` feeds messages in and reads state out. This separation makes the ledger logic directly unit-testable (as `TestBackgroundLedger` and `test_is_own_result` demonstrate) without a fake SDK client, and keeps `sdk_session.py` focused on the transport concern. The `WAITED_TASK_TYPES` constant mirrors the SDK's private `DEFERRING_TASK_TYPES` with a comment explaining the redeclaration, which is the right call for an internal SDK symbol.

findings.title: Session rotation failure leaves a visible unusable state rather than a half-alive client
findings.description: The `_reconnect` method wraps `connect()` in a try/except that records `unusable_reason` on failure and re-raises. Every subsequent `dispatch`, `compact`, and `seed_context` call hits `_require_usable()` first, which raises `ProviderError` with the stored reason. This prevents the dangerous "old client disconnected, new client failed to connect, but the session object still looks usable" state. The `TestUnusableSessionInBatch` test in `test_executor_each.py` exercises the full path: a failed rotate reconnect inside an `each` loop causes subsequent items to be flagged with "SDK session unusable" in the batch report and logged at WARNING, and the fresh client's `query` is never called.

findings.title: Idle-timeout stop path is observable and best-effort with correct failure semantics
findings.description: When the background idle timeout fires, `_stop_background` iterates every tracked agent ID, calls `stop_task`, and logs at ERROR (via `logger.exception`) on individual failures while continuing to the next ID. It then clears the ledger locally (since a lost terminal signal is exactly the case where the SDK may not have delivered one) and logs a WARNING with the idle duration and agent descriptions. The `except Exception` with `# noqa: BLE001` is justified by the inline comment: the SDK raises a bare `Exception` both for stop-control timeouts and CLI errors, so no narrower type exists, and stopping is cleanup where log-and-continue is the correct semantics. The test `test_stop_task_failure_is_logged_and_next_id_still_stopped` verifies that a failed stop on the first ID still stops the second and produces exactly one ERROR log with the task ID and traceback.

findings.title: Resume seeding refactor preserves behavior while enabling lazy-session seeding
findings.description: The old inline resume-seeding block in `execute_pipeline` is extracted to `_load_resume_seed`, which returns the seed text or `None` and logs at INFO when it finds one. The seeding then happens either immediately (connected session → `seed_context`) or deferred to the lazy connect (`_connect_lazy_session(seed=resume_seed)`). The `resume_seed = None` after either path ensures a second lazy connect never re-seeds. The `test_resume_seeds_lazy_session_at_connect` and `test_resume_without_summary_passes_no_seed_to_lazy_session` tests verify both the seed-is-passed and seed-is-None cases through the real executor with a mocked `_connect_lazy_session`. The pre-existing `test_resume_seeds_from_compact_summary` confirms the connected-session path still calls `seed_context` with the correct text and `SeedSource.RESUME`.

findings.title: Bool config coercion and typed-read overload are correct and well-tested
findings.description: The `_coerce_bool` function accepts a reasonable set of true/false spellings (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed) and raises `ValueError` with the key name and accepted values on failure. The `get_typed_config` overloads add a `bool` signature with the implementation correctly checking `type_ is bool` before `type_ is int` (with the comment "bool is a subclass of int"). The test matrix in `TestBoolConfigValues` covers all accepted spellings, the invalid-spelling error, the typed read returning a native `bool`, and the typed read rejecting a TOML `1` (which `tomllib` parses as `int`, not `bool`) with the expected `ValueError`. The CLI test `test_invalid_value_exits_with_error` confirms `sq config set pipeline.auto_memory maybe` exits 1 with "must be a boolean".

findings.title: Review result `system_prompt_mode` and `setting_sources` replace the old bool with a proper enum and always render
findings.description: The old `default_system_prompt_preset_used: bool` is replaced by `system_prompt_mode: SystemPromptMode | None` and `setting_sources: str | None`. The `to_dict` method includes both keys unconditionally (null when not reported, matching the `stop_reason` convention). The Run Digest in `persistence.py` always renders both lines (`_render_optional` gives "not computed" for `None`). The `-vv` appendix's preset annotation now keys on `result.system_prompt_mode in _PRESET_MODES` (a frozenset of `PRESET` and `PRESET_APPEND`) rather than the old bool. The `TestPromptAndSettingsDigestLines` tests parametrize over all four `SystemPromptMode` values and verify each renders in the correct position, and the JSON test confirms both keys are present with correct values. The old `default_system_prompt_preset_used` field is fully removed — `grep` confirms no remaining readers in `src/` or `tests/`.

findings.title: Template `setting_sources` is now never-None, closing the accidental CLI-default-settings hole
findings.description: The `ReviewTemplate.setting_sources` field changed from `list[str] | None` to `list[str]`, and `_resolve_setting_sources` maps absent/null YAML to `list(REVIEW_SETTING_SOURCES)` (`["project"]`) while preserving an explicit `[]` as `[]`. This closes the D9 hole where a template without a `setting_sources` key left the field `None`, which the SDK provider interpreted as "no `--setting-sources` flag", which the CLI interpreted as "load user + project settings". The `test_every_builtin_template_uses_project` test parametrizes over the actual template directory and asserts `["project"]` for each. The `test_custom_template_resolution` test covers missing, null, empty-list, and explicit-list cases. The `test_non_list_value_is_rejected` test confirms a non-list value raises `TemplateValidationError`.

findings.title: One-shot dispatch telemetry now includes prompt and settings keys derived from the actual config
findings.description: The `telemetry` dict is initialized from `describe_run_settings(config, is_sdk=is_sdk)` rather than an empty dict, so `system_prompt_mode`, `setting_sources`, and `auto_memory` are always present. Tool keys are still only added when tools were given (the `tools_given` metadata check in the response loop). The docstring was updated to reflect this: "The tool keys are absent when the run had no tools… The prompt and settings keys (slice 932 D12) are always present, derived from the config actually spawned." The `test_sdk_one_shot_records_prompt_and_settings` test verifies the three keys are present with correct values for an SDK dispatch with an explicit system prompt, and `test_non_sdk_one_shot_system_prompt_is_the_whole_prompt` confirms the non-SDK path records `custom` mode. The `test_summary_one_shot_records_empty_prompt_and_settings` test confirms the summary path records `empty`/`none`/`False` for its config.

findings.title: Dispatch session path correctly rejects per-step `system_prompt` with an actionable error
findings.description: The guard `if context.params.get("system_prompt")` returns a failed `ActionResult` with a clear error message explaining that the session's system prompt is fixed at connect time and cannot be changed per step, and suggesting either a non-SDK model or removing the `system_prompt`. This is the same pattern as the existing `allowed_tools` guard just above it. The `test_session_path_rejects_step_system_prompt` test verifies the error message contains both "declares 'system_prompt'" and "fixed at connect time", and that `session.dispatch` is never called.

findings.title: `tail_text` utility is correct, tested, and used consistently at both D6 and D7 call sites
findings.description: `tail_text` collapses whitespace, returns `(empty response)` for empty/whitespace-only input, keeps short text as-is, and returns the last `FINAL_TEXT_TAIL_CHARS` (400) with a `…` prefix for longer text. The four tests in `test_text_tail.py` cover all branches. It is used in two production call sites: `dispatch_artifact.py` (appending the agent's final text to the missing-artifact error, D7) and `sdk_session.py` (logging a discarded leftover follow-up turn, D6). Both use sites call `tail_text(response)` where `response` is the dispatch's `outputs["response"]` string, which is the correct input.

findings.title: New tests use real SDK message types rather than MagicMocks for the session fakes
findings.description: The `ScriptedClient` and its helper functions (`sdk_text`, `sdk_result`, `sdk_task_started`, etc.) construct real `AssistantMessage`, `ResultMessage`, `TaskStartedMessage`, `TaskNotificationMessage`, and `TaskUpdatedMessage` instances from the `claude_agent_sdk` package. This is important because the production code (`sdk_turns.py`) uses `isinstance` checks against these real types — a `MagicMock(spec=...)` would not survive `isinstance(msg, TaskStartedMessage)` unless the spec was set correctly, and even then the `.task_id`, `.task_type`, `.description` attributes would need to be individually configured. Using real dataclass instances with the correct field values is more faithful and less brittle. The `scripted_session` helper wraps a `ScriptedClient` in a real `SDKExecutionSession`, so the dispatch code under test is the real `dispatch` → `_collect_turns` → `_read_turn` chain, not a mock.

findings.title: The `sq serve` and audit paths are correctly unaffected by the auto-memory change
findings.description: In `provider.py`, `sdk_settings_options` is called with `config.setting_sources or []` and `auto_memory=config.auto_memory`. For `sq serve` callers (`server/routes/agents.py`), `AgentConfig` is created without `setting_sources` or `auto_memory`, so they default to `None` and `False`. The provider then sets `kwargs["env"]` with the auto-memory disable var (because `auto_memory=False`) but does NOT set `kwargs["setting_sources"]` (because `config.setting_sources is None`). This preserves the existing `sq serve` behavior where the API caller supplies their own config and the CLI uses its default setting sources. The audit path (`metrology/audit.py`) explicitly sets `setting_sources=["project"]` and does not set `auto_memory` (defaults to `False`), so it gets auto-memory off as designed. The `test_settings_policy.py` test matrix covers both paths and asserts the expected sources and auto-memory flag.
